en: // The Praise in a Garland of Metres //

The masters of speech declare that *vṛtta* is of three kinds—equal, half-equal, and unequal—for the sake of accomplishing the welfare of others; in brief it is threefold, but in detail it is infinite.
Wherein the supreme sages have sung the very names established in their specific forms, and wherein the meter and the words shine forth through various arrangements; // JVms_2 //

Even by observing the corresponding forms, the wise are able to calculate the weights and lightnesses of all the steps in their proper sequence; what further need is there for inquiry into this matter?
May that which is being contemplated with reverence— the singular ornament of the speech of those born into the lineage of the virtuous— be effective for the destruction of your delusions.
// Prologue //
The source of wisdom, speech,
and fortune.
She who shines as the sole ground of her own self.
And it is constantly attended by those who proclaim its virtues.
By the stains of stumbling from their common support, as they arise among the gods, asuras, and others. // JVms_8 //
By those who properly maintain the excellence of awakening, which has been increased through practice throughout many lifetimes.
Among meters, the Gītā is like the Gāyatrī, the first among those esteemed by the virtuous;
it is that in which the future welfare of the world truly resides.
Victorious is this slender-waisted form of the Teacher, who holds a blue lotus in his hand and whose abode is grace.
Be gracious, O Blessed One; look with favor for a moment upon this dull-witted person who has you as his sole refuge.
Having encountered your teaching of the Sugata, it blazes intensely;
for heat, when exceeding its limit, becomes as unbearable as the radiance of the sun.
Even though they display youthful sports to their heart's content,
O Youth, the body of the Victors remains truly youthful in its grace.
From that [meditation], even for one who merely recollects it, there arises for the multitude of beings a form that has shaken off all lower states and is directed toward the higher realms.
Through the extensive praise of whose qualities, the wise, having risen up, utter a single verse in the *anuṣṭubh* meter that is free from attachment and points toward the supreme state.
For those whose eyes of wisdom were obstructed by the darkness of terrible delusion,
she was like a lamp on a jeweled staff for all people.

O Lord of all leaders, with respect to the wealth of the Great Sage which surpasses that of the three worlds, even our own authoritative means of knowledge flash forth as being nothing other than that very [wealth].
In this lineage of the Perfectly Awakened Ones, which is mature in its burning away and destruction of intense afflictions,
this [work] bears an ornament and shines, just as a garland of lightning flashes in a cloud.
O World-Child, the playful grace of your true guru shines forth as if he were holding a staff of betel to teach you the science of political ethics.
The palm of your hand, with its trembling sprout-like fingers, rivals the vast intellect that proclaims its own course throughout the three worlds.
O Sovereign Lord, your speech, with its variegated words, brings about the attainment of the essence of reality simultaneously with the universe itself.
In that vast and magnificent splendor, some attain a firm footing;
there, even their sidelong glance, having found its mark, finds rest for a moment.
Through being cultivated by one such as you, this people has attained excellence;
it shines like the earth when it is continuously ploughed with the face of the plow.
O Giver of Boons, for indeed that transformation is produced by you within this [speech],
since the seed of your word, once sown, bears fruit in the form of peace.
O Lord, who indeed is capable here of measuring your deeds,
which are like the tracks of a young serpent in the water during a time of thick darkness?
However, O Lord, the bliss born from hearing of your fame destroys my steadfastness,
as it casts away the seal upon the faces of the world that had been set by their own assumption of maturity.

O Abode of Śrī, your body— skillful in playful pastimes and having reached the further shore of knowledge and conduct— shines in the row of the sons of the Buddha like a lotus among water-born flowers.
I bow to you, the mountain of the rising of the lineage of the Udgīta, the light of wisdom seated upon the chariot of skillful means,
the master in shattering dullness, the sun for the lotus-stalk of the three worlds.
O Lord, the splendor of the sons of the Buddhas shines intensely through your prosperity,
like the golden summit of a particular mountain, radiant with the luster of jewel-sprouts.
O Lord, the multitude of the virtuous wanders about with joy, spreading your all-encompassing cry of victory and illuminating the world, like a drum being beaten everywhere for a proclamation.

O wise one, through the union with the honey of your virtues— the glory of whose lotus-like head is the foremost among the hosts of disputants— your speech, like a goddess intoxicated by the three worlds, delights even the steadfast.
In you, the ornament of the lineage of the Jinas who turn the wheel of the universe,
that state called "youth"— which is considered by the female parrots to be like a peacock— is clearly fading away.
The series of ornaments upon each limb of yours— garlanded with rays from various jewels and possessing a burgeoning wealth of its own luster— has brought the *śuddhavirāṭ* meter itself into defeat.
O Lord of Debaters, may your hand protect the world as it brandishes the gesture during the exposition of the method of reality—
its bracelets trembling from the beautiful resonance produced by its striking against [the opponent's] arguments.

Then, beholding this entire world— surpassing all else, bearing its own resting place within its own domain— the *triṣṭubh* meter, as it were, became sluggish before your form, your multitude of virtues, and your fame.
O Lord, whose body is like the moon rising with vast compassion and possesses a continuous stream of shimmering,
incomparable luster— whom does this most auspicious form of yours not bring joy?
This stainless, pure white [lineage] of yours, equal in luster to the multitude of rays from the autumnal moon,
shines within your heart like a string of pearls— the very manifestation of your accumulated virtues.
This [jasmine] of yours shines as if it were the fame of your noble birth, victory, and benevolence being sung;
for it seems to offer a welcome with the humming of swarms of bees, drawn by the fragrance wafting from afar.
Possessing a vast fragrance, like a reservoir of honey, she bears an abundance of the fourfold paste (cātus-sama) as if it were a cosmetic powder;
she is the splendor of the blue lotus, reclining happily upon her petals, with the playful movements of bees that never cease.
Through his cultivation of the elixir of beauty, he is to be highly honored above all as Vāsava himself, by whom the pair of eyes—
free from blinking and devoid of darkness— has been regained for a long time.
With their hands joined in *añjali* and wearing crowns adorned with the jewels of the *Haktyāna* [Vajrayāna], these fortunate ones, filled with joy,
have long attended upon your two feet, which are free from the influence of other [worldly] authorities.
O Lord of the Intellect, what is the use of Indra’s power, or even of the glory of Brahmā, or of wealth that surpasses them? If your lotus feet are present, everything is fully accomplished.
In this difficult passage of birth, those two fierce ones— karma and affliction— acting together, will surely lead one who is averse to serving you to destruction,
just as a violent wind and a wave destroy a ship in the middle of the ocean.
For those whose minds perceive afar and who are free from fault, some indescribable mental continuum flashes forth—
unceasingly until the end of existence— aroused by the longing to attend upon you.
When there is the swift attainment of the four noble truths— the nectar that puts an end to the heart’s delusions—
there arises, even from a mere glance of your side-long look, a certain state of merit characterized by mature wisdom.
The fame of you, whose abode is the hymn of praise, which surpasses all other abodes and delights the hearts of the virtuous,
whitens the ten directions like pale sandalwood moistened by the thick moonlight of the full moon.
With its many crests rising high, the mountain form— its perception of solidity difficult to abandon because it has taken refuge in you—
follows its own destruction like one split by the fierce stroke of Indra’s thunderbolt.
Seated upon a lofty lion-throne, worthy of the sovereign power of the Dharma that has flourished,
you are attended by those whose splendor is auspicious— Śiva, Upendra, Vajrāyudha, and Vedhas.
May your feet be graced with the characteristics just described and may they be within your range;
for those blessed *upajātis* of the gods, whose verses possess the elaborate artistry of *śravya-yati*, are truly fortunate.
Without doubt, even though there are other sovereigns who emulate all your personal qualities to their heart's content,
those lords— conquerors of the bodiless god of love— desire you as their lineage-holder with an intellect that admits no other.
I bow to Vāgīśvara, who has the form of a youth adorned with lovely and variegated ornaments, who is golden-hued, whose crest is graced by Akṣobhya,
who possesses the splendor of the rising sun for the lineage of the Lord of Sages, and who embodies the very essence of eloquence.

O Lord, even with words of extreme length, those of sweet voice cannot reach the further shore of Your virtues; therefore, O Blessed One, this praise of mine, though composed of few syllables, is indeed auspicious, as it generates nothing but my own joy.
O Lord of Speech, the Goddess of Eloquence— whose every ornament shines brilliantly, who has risen from the lotus-faces of the meritorious,
who is radiant by her very nature, and who wears a garland of excellent virtues— approaches you of her own accord.
The arrows of the five-arrowed god have been brought to ruin; the fire of hatred has been extinguished, and the dullness born of delusion has been cast away.
O Lord, whose form is intent upon bestowing grace upon the three worlds, the prosperity of the Viśvedevas has indeed been attained by you alone.

Filled within with the various jewels of your multitude of virtues, you bear the likeness of a garland of clouds from the ocean of space; through your extreme fortitude, you act as a rain-cloud with showers of the true Dharma-water that extinguishes the fire of afflictions.

O Supreme One, before you, the esteemed opponents—terrified and disoriented—regard even your speech, whether rapid or measured, as something easily met with the state of being mute; yet they hold it in high esteem.
Purifying all three worlds with a radiance as white as the rays of the moon,
your fame endures for a long time, just as the Mandākinī flows eternally from the summit of the celestial mountain.
O abode of compassion, this fame of yours, which dwells in the hearts of the virtuous,
utterly captivates them in every direction, like a blooming jasmine creeper covering the ground with its mass of blossoms.
This certain ocean of compassion, who possesses a collection of acquired splendors, dispels the misfortunes of the worlds;
he is skillful in manifesting many tens of millions of Buddhas and maintains the playful grace of Vāgīśvara within the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
Scattering, as it were, masses of light with the brilliance of the shimmering waves of the celestial river,
your sword, dark as the waters of the Yamunā, shines eternally within its scabbard.
O Lord, sovereign of supreme beauty, where is this form of yours, so lovely with its enchanting strings of pearls;
and where is that [other form] which moves like a serpent, adorned with terrifying ornaments, for the sake of pacifying beings who are exceedingly difficult to subdue?
O Lord, whose mind is not captivated by this form of yours, adorned with a profusion of closely set pearls, which is like a fresh garland of exquisite jasmine flowers fit for seasonal worship? 63.

O Lord, if the world’s eye, greedy to behold your auspicious form, were to abandon its weariness in the ocean of the nectar of your supreme luster and wander everywhere with a whirring sound, O Body! [it would find no rest].
O Giver of Boons, it is evident that your limbs possess the quality of renunciation; O One who has transcended existence, they will surely become ours.
This pair of ear-cavities, a vessel for drinking the nectar of your words, is the cause of our joy.

I choose this one boon from you, O you of incomparable power: that no person like me may take refuge even in you, for such a one would find detachment from the nectar-like essence of tranquility and would fall into the haughty conduct of the dull-witted.

O Moon, by the power of the merit arising from your grace, the virtuous person attains the bliss that pierces the eightfold [sheaths], and through the acts that bring joy to the eyes of embodied beings, he reaches the path of liberation.

O King of Speakers, those fortunate ones whose essence of wisdom is obtained by taking refuge at your feet do not have their memory impaired, even throughout the entire course of existence, by the various causes such as the excesses of pleasure and pain.

O you whose mind is honored for its renowned virtues, for those who delight in serving your feet, a certain bliss arises in the form of creative activity— blazing with the removal of the entire mass of impurities and esteemed throughout the world.
With a body as lovely as refined gold and possessing supreme grace,
he who is served by the excellent female swan of eloquent speech is celebrated here as Mañjughoṣa— your [teacher], the singular royal swan upon the lotus-pond of the Conqueror’s mind.
If even a minute interruption were clearly difficult to achieve regarding these three unbearable afflictions,
O Protector, where indeed could such a form as yours— delighting the eyes and minds of the three worlds— be found here?
If one were to bring about the cessation of the waters in the ocean— the repository of jewels with their shimmering masses of great rays—
and if such a beautiful continuity of luster were observed in the body of one like you, then this [splendor] would be truly radiant.

O Lord, when you, who delight the worthy ones, emit delightful streams of nectar with deep resonances and shine forth intensely, that very *yati* (caesura) follows the rain-cloud with extreme charm and clarity; thus it is the *mattamayūra* meter.

This creeper, which has emerged from the flowers that are your beautiful eyes, triumphs like a vine arising from a blue lotus tree in the springtime; it produces unsurpassed joy for the three worlds and speaks with the sweet sound of bees intoxicated by honey.

We consider your conduct alone to be the ornament of the Victor’s doctrine— a *vasantatilaka* verse that is like a fresh mango blossom, being sung by swarms of learned bees who have attained joy through being filled with qualities that surpass all others.

I offer profound salutation to the tutelary deity of the assembly of disputants— him who is mounted upon the back of a lion whose face is turned directly toward him, who is the root of supreme prosperity and possesses a heart of intense compassion, and whose beautiful feet are as lovely as refined gold.
O Sage, for you who partake of the nectar of samādhi— an immaculate intellect flowing forth, free from all obscurations and with every conceptual proliferation stilled—
your unconquered ascetic discipline, which has destroyed the prowess of your enemies, subdues the three worlds.
Out of compassion, for the sake of pacifying the merciless conduct of those with terrifying forms,
your row of club-like arms shines forth somewhere, bearing various flower-buds of weapons despite their extreme ferocity.
O Giver of Boons, for those who long for the enjoyment of the highest good, the undistracted withdrawal from sense objects, the destruction of Māra, the attainment of welfare for the three worlds,
and that state which is difficult to reach and cannot be taken away— there is no other direction than devotion to you that is free from obstruction.
If someone with senses restrained and a mind steady through devotion meditates anywhere upon even a fraction of you,
this earth— adorned by the girdle of the ocean— will surely soon choose that person for herself.
Even though their garments were shaken off, the celestial women wore their bodices torn by the swelling horripilation shimmering with perspiration;
in your assembly, O Lord, they display this expansion of passion, intense with trembling and as if enchanting with its luster, composed of the *atiśakvarī* meter.
Victorious is this body, whose incomparable and lovely grace in its limbs steals away all delight in other forms of sublime beauty;
it is a garland of radiance, the supreme abode of victory over the splendor of the unbroken hosts of Indras.

In your assemblies, O one who has joyfully taken up the burden of the Jina, your speech— charming with the fifth note (*pañcama*) accompanied by lutes whose sweet, low, and melodious sounds are blended with the rhythmic beat of flawless cymbals— speaks this *madraka* dance-song, which desires its own glory.

Victorious is your tree-like arm, O Lord, adorned with armlets resembling a network of chains used to immobilize the world-conquering elephant; it is a great bolt against the path of misfortune, the crusher of the pride of Māra, and the beloved of the Sugata.

O Lord, the digit of the moon in autumn truly emulates your splendor— splendor that has arisen from the greatness of your honored virtues at the peak of existence, which is pure and free from all stains, and which has accumulated through your supreme victory.

This garland, possessing the essence of nectar, fashioned by the young wives of the Lord of the Immortals, rests upon your head; it is delightful with its intense fragrance that attracts swarms of young bees, and it is a source of bliss perfectly suited for the Sugata.
Because you do not tread the path of an ascetic, yet through your exceedingly generous intellect you spread throughout the world deeds that benefit others,
the sky— possessing the luster of a mass of snow— produces for you a multitude of qualities that surpass its own natural jewels.

O You whose multitude of virtues is immeasurable, how could even the most eloquent speech ever reach its end? For the collection of Your supreme qualities exceeds the mass of jewels in the oceans, even by ascetics of perfect discipline who have measured them out.
Victorious is this body of yours, O you of vast compassion, which, like the earth, sustains the entire world;
here it remains with unwavering fortitude, enduring the manifold difficulties of all people who are as fickle as children and who mock the ordinances of fate.

O you whose accumulation of auspiciousness is gentle yet possesses exceedingly great compassion, even your mind, though soft, perceives that the lotus of the Jina lineage— held like a blue lotus in the palm of your hand— is free from uneven weight, even for one of dull intellect.

O Lord, you shall display here within the belly of the world’s forest the noble *ṛṣabhagajavilasita* gait— [a gait] which makes the pride of the multitude of arrogant elephants of rival disputants, fickle due to their inability to grasp the fragrance of your fame scattered through the sky, roar like a thundercloud that has conquered all others.

O you who have shattered your vow while clad in armor for the sake of bestowing the welfare of the world, where is there even a trace of distress for the women of Māra? For their hands remain languidly engaged in painting decorative leaf-designs upon the lovely surfaces of their cheeks.
O Lord whose peerless and beautiful form has been seen by the Victors, these eight [world-protectors] are moved even more intensely by you, O dispeller of sorrow.
This youthful grace, radiant with the five-fold silken garments and adorned by a row of toenails like white lotuses of excellent merit, delights them.
"How may the *atyaṣṭi* meter of my virtues prevail here over all worlds?"— thus did your own poetic meter freely undergo its transformation,
so that within you alone has arisen this prosperity, which brings about the discernment of the supreme flavor and is the mountain-peak of every branch of happiness.

Victorious is the Lord of the Three Worlds, the Upholder of the Earth, whose broad chest is like the stone floor of the celestial mansions of the immortals; whose splendor from his feet resembles a forest of lotuses on the ground; who is adorned with a manifest brilliance exceeding a hundred suns; and who crushes the pride of Death.

O Youthful Sun of the Conqueror’s lineage, if you have not for long taken heed of the joy that comes from taking refuge at the lotus-feet of your own feet— a joy for those shrouded by the dense veil of the darkness of delusion who dwell in the perils of existence that exceed even the depths of the subterranean caves— then the Māras have triumphed.
O Lord, this fickle life, which has been ordained as if it were the great fruit produced over a hundred kalpas by those devoted to bowing before you,

is like a lotus fallen upon a leaf— though it had attained the state of being a worthy ornament— when it encounters the lineage of the sky-faring ones who possess profound compassion for those who seek refuge.
O Giver of Boons, it is only the benevolent face of Brahmā that brings forth the majesty of your speech, purified by its affection for the expansion of your virtues;
and it is he who, accompanied by the *yajus* hymns—the abode of the *sāman* consisting of nectar—produces the very temple of pride for the nectar of your fame.
Your noble conduct—which bestows joy upon the three worlds—attains the state of a blossoming mango tree within the honey of the Jina’s resolve;

it is graced by the humming of the bees that are the ascetics, who are uplifted by the joyful drinking of the nectar of tranquility from the blossoms of the sacred teachings, and it possesses the sweet warbling of the cuckoos that are your eloquent utterances.

O Lord Sugata, mountain of the earth, whose deep cave-abode crushes the elephants of the pride of many disputants; O Sovereign of the forest of the three worlds, the fierce great army of Māra, though restrained by the ocean of the flavor of your playful sport, flees repeatedly like a doe out of fear of you.

O Lord of renowned valor, for the sake of subduing those who are difficult to tame, you sometimes assume a form out of the force of your compassion, at the tip of whose foot this triple world—its sole activity being wailing with cries of pain upon hearing its name—goes to dissolution; it does not quickly regain its composure, O Master.
That perfection of splendor which would have arisen on the head of the wish-fulfilling tree bearing an auspicious jar resembling a beautiful fruit has now been produced by the single preceptor;
and this vine-like arm of the Master, shining with the fingernails of his hand as it moves during his exposition, gleams like a flowering creeper swaying in the wind.

If this poem, composed by the treasury of the moon-like arts that leaves no blemish upon the entire family of Buddhas, has been placed in your heart, then you have truly become a necklace for the great dull-witted.
If it has been embraced by your tongue with the essence of camphor, has it not indeed served as an ear-ornament that shatters the jeweled earring?
O Lord of incomparable majesty, whose accumulation of merit has been so well-heaped that you seem insatiable even with services as pleasant as the palm of Śacī’s hand—
your forehead, marked with a clearly visible tamāla-leaf design upon its jeweled footstool-slab, bows down before the hundred-fold bearer of the earth (Indra).

O Lord, for those who remain steadfast for the sake of others and possess supreme fortitude, I shall proclaim—having heard it from the mouth of the Compassionate One toward the universe—a state that is a mine of various aesthetic flavors;
O Teacher, grant me even for a moment that purifying condition of the pure, by which you strike down the pervasive darknesses of my flashing sins.
May Mañjuśrī protect you—he who is like the moon for the increase of the ocean of the noble lineage of the Buddhas; who has surpassed all talk of the god of love in his union with the lady Prajñā;
and who, in the battle against the deer-like afflictions of the world, assumes the prowess of a tiger, wielding the restraint of the sun to overcome the night of terrifying delusions.
Seeing the state of your victory over the three worlds, the hosts of gods and sages—whose fierce planets had been blunted and whose body hairs stood on end like sprouts of fear—were shattered.

Then, from the lunar orb of your face, which possesses a priceless smile as its wealth and is surrounded by the moonlight of your purest teeth, you acted for the benefit of all who love you out of compassion, even though you were already intent upon it.

May the lion’s sport of yours bring about the destruction of Māra throughout the world—a sport that serves as a companion to the gods who, terrified by fear, seek refuge from afar with their feathers spread wide; which manifests the minds of those separated from their lovers as filled with intense devotion; which possesses the immeasurable speed of the sky; whose roar exceeds the thundering of clouds at the end of an eon; and which shatters Māra on all sides.

O Supreme One among those who teach that there is perpetual non-abiding in both saṃsāra and nirvāṇa, you are rich in true compassion for the immeasurable realm of sentient beings who are distressed by unbearable suffering; with a mind that is utterly pure like the autumnal sky and pervades the entire universe, such a conduct as yours is not attained even by name by any other.

By the lords of the four quarters, whose entire hosts depend on the momentary restraint of your side-long glances—which resemble streaks of iron melted by intense heat—and who are by nature ever-striving;

and by the company of beautiful women, who have conquered the five-arrowed god of love through their vast display of amorous charms and possess ten-fold beauty—you spread a certain splendor of exceeding wonder.

The sky is filled with the splendor of your worship, appearing as if carved from a mass of blossoming *kunda* flowers by the graceful curves of the three parts of the eyes; it seems repeatedly bathed by the luster of your beloved’s beauty that washes away the body-paint with its sweat; and it is pervaded by Vidyādhara women whose ignorance has been dispelled, who wear garlands made radiant by swarms of bees humming with joy as they are drawn by the fragrance.

O Lord, O Ocean of Virtues, O Teacher beyond the reach of words, this song of mine is surely for the sake of those traveling the path of worldly existence who always sing Your name—O Master whose fame is celebrated to the ends of the earth as pure and more beautiful than the autumnal moon, and who possesses the excellence of form, birth, conduct, power, and progressive majesty—and may they easily attain that very fame. O Lord of Speech, O Giver of Boons, though you know your own power, you alone— having offered up the sacrifice of total renunciation toward wealth and sensual objects— experience in heaven the splendor of amorous play, which is the sole abode of delight, where swarms of bees are noisy with intense rut as they emerge from bathing in the essence of honey, and which causes even the hearts of sages to waver.

O Treasure of Strength, this army—darkened by the masses of rutting elephants whose deep trumpeting has surpassed the roar of towering clouds; with its throngs of foot-soldiers enveloped in the radiance of the rays from all its sharpened weapons;

featuring excellent warriors mounted upon superior chariots; and graced by noble horses that move with a captivating gait as they enter the fray—seeks refuge in you alone, O Man, who are the sole resort for those in need.

O Lord, he who dwells on earth with his intellect subdued, whose wrong views are dispelled, and who constantly remembers You— the abode of bliss, renowned for granting noble boons and supreme residence— shall find that, when the final stage has dawned,
a slender, moon-faced woman, delightful with the intervals of the rising fifth note accompanied by the play of youth, shall become subject to him along with the royal fortune.

O Lord, that lake on earth—whose waters are like the supreme state of Vasu, whose internal organ is devoted solely to the welfare of all, and which bears Your name—becomes a place of perfected residence for the Creator;

it is fragrant with the scent of ichor flowing from the temples of the elephants of the quarters as they plunge in, and its golden lotus groves are filled with swarms of bees and the footprints of cranes, swans, and curlews.

O Destroyer of Darkness, O Foe of Māra, O Slayer of Evil, O Ornament of the Earth for the Sons of the Victors! O Mountain-born One, whose splendor of beauty unfolds in full maturity at your creation; O Source of Stability, O Dispeller of Existence, O You of Noble Prowess! O Giver of Boons, the fruitless worship undertaken toward you distresses even the wise, as it manifests here—though one may be attached to enjoyments—as the unrestrained expansion of the serpent that is the body of the most formidable objects of sense.

That which spreads clearly, incessantly, and immeasurably around the limbs like drops of the essence of nectar; which, arising from constant contemplation, is the locus of the flavor of the nine rasas, peerless and of incomparable splendor;

which is not easily obtained even through other various methods of meritorious deeds despite great effort—the fruit of the tree of service to You, which one experiences here when the self is devoted, is known as the "removal of all calamities."

Victory, victory to the playful grace of the Lord of the Lotus Dance, whose form throbs with the sport of beautiful compassion! There, the cloud—driven by the fierce winds from the mass of your unrestrained staff-like arms, and appearing like a single staff for the three worlds at the time of universal dissolution as it moves through a torrential rain—seems to bestow relief from exhaustion upon you, while its belly is filled with hissing serpents rising from the depths of Pātāla, which are pressed down by your feet that move with restless gait.

O Giver of Boons, your excellence of radiance— praised with great joy by the noblest of Āryas who have attained the final form through the purification of each step here and the cultivation of the three syllables of samādhi— is such that even the oceans, elephants, clouds, pleasure-pools, and the wild conch-shells, sounding their approval with hearts never satiated, do not grow weary. This is because they are filled with the essence of the proclamation of rejoicing [in your deeds].

O Lord, whose limbs possess the fortune of a fully blossomed golden lotus, who have bestowed the city of Nirvāṇa upon those seeking refuge in the darkness for the sake of establishing peace in the three worlds,

and who are the foremost among the sons of the Daśabala— by you, the destroyer of suffering, when praised by Bhavāri who has assumed the form of a Tamāla tree out of devotion, a great heap of merit has been accumulated; may that same prosperity accrue to the entire multitude of living beings.

I too, my internal darkness having been suppressed by a mind entirely devoted to the propitiation of your lotus feet, having realized the non-dual reality— which pervades the multitude of all things and consists of the innate nature of dreams and illusions— shall move through the three worlds as long as even a single person remains unliberated; with my vigor aroused by the power of compassion for those who lack it, and with my various activities engaged solely in the task of supreme benefit to others, I shall remain until the mass of gem-like rays from the crests of the beautiful gods, serpents, and lords of the Daityas rests upon the edge of your footstool, which shines like a vast, blossoming land-lotus.

Victorious is this Youth, the Lord of Speech, a treasure-house of wondrous conduct whose tireless labor brings solace to the three worlds when their power is overturned and seized by the unbearable, unrestrained fire of suffering; he is the radiant ornament of the pure lineage of the Fully Awakened Ones, spreading his fame that fills the intermediate spaces; and he is delightful in his firm resolve to utterly destroy the army of the irrepressible heroes of Māra, having brought to full maturity the rising tide of his profound majesty.

I pay homage to the Lord who possesses the power of compassion, the abode of pure qualities, whose body is incomparably fierce yet filled with profound, hidden wonder; who is immersed in the great non-dual ocean; whose conduct is graced by the noble aesthetic flavor of the new drama; whose armor for conquering the world is the network of horripilation shimmering from the embrace of his mature consort, the Lady Vajra; who terrifies all gods and demons with his formidable, loud laughter released through the intoxication of drinking the thick blood and marrow of his victims; and who is the embodiment of the strength of mercy. (Thus ends the section on the varieties of difficult feats.)
In the *Mālāstutivivṛti*, the even meters (*samavṛtta*).
Bearing on one half the luster of the moon, free from childishness, and on the other half the luster of the rising sun,
whose mind would not be deeply moved by this body of yours that acts under the sway of compassion?

O you who have heard the teachings on the Destroyer of Existence (Śiva), one must quickly attain the experience of your feet—whether through the particular satisfaction derived from the nectar-essence of reality, or by virtue of the accomplishment of all desired goals. 126.

O All-pervading Lord, what more do the wise desire? If one were to know that [the state of] his body would become like a leap of a deer, made radiant by the luster of a shimmering necklace through the stream of the nectar-essence of Your glance.
This splendor of her face, having attained the essence of the flavor of vast compassion through the power of her own innate wisdom,
shines like a blossoming golden lotus bud with its shimmering petal-like lips, its tip in full bloom.
This other face of yours shines like a mass of blooming blue lotuses;
it captivates the mind like an *aparavaktra* verse, as if risen with the splendor of white water-lilies.
Alas, this conduct of yours, though victorious over the three worlds, appears to me to be only half-equal;
for in certain matters, even this charming play of yours is like that of a child, devoid of all worldly purpose.
Having beheld for a moment that single foot of yours which forcibly overcomes the summit of the three worlds,
how could the Goddess of Speech not become your affectionate servant, like a maidservant?
Why indeed would you cast aside even your intellects— which have naturally arrived at the bed of tranquility—
through hundreds of most wondrous and difficult deeds, were it not for your impetuous compassion?

O Bhadravirāṭ, may your auspicious body— the abode of all excellence, whose beauty is characterized by auspicious marks visible upon every limb— extend blessings even as it has passed from the memory of the world.

Your form shines forth, bannered with the thunderbolt, lotus, sword, jewel, and discus— splendid rays of light that quiver on all sides, which are delightful and whose ultimate purpose is the welfare of others.
In that which consists solely of mental states, where could such a supreme fulfillment of the welfare of others be cultivated except in compassion?

Therefore, this [compassion] is designated by the same term as the feminine form of the possessive suffix *matup* through the deceptive appearance of its [the word "compassion"] form, owing to the sound of its constituent parts.

Victorious is this exceedingly beautiful body of yours, O Transcendent One, which mocks the stainless golden moon with its surrounding mass of rays like the rising dawn, and which is skillful in creating delight for the entire world.

Victorious is your crest-lock, O Cloud of Attainment! It is an abode of the excellence of its well-fashioned construction, inlaid with a multitude of pure jewels that serve as companions to the images of the Blessed Sugata—the Lord whose majesty is the weight of serving his feet, which are so difficult for the three worlds to reach. It possesses a resonance resembling the tinkling of the bracelets on the arms of the gods who delight in imitating the sound of the drum that proclaims the Jina’s method; it is a treasury of the humming of swarms of bees gathering from the fragrance of the celestial flowers of the gods. 137.

Victorious is your eye and speech, O Lord—the eye that, directed toward the truth of origination, speaks of the various causes of arising for those whose interest has been well-awakened; and the speech that, finding great delight in those whose minds savor the essence of the bliss of peace, proclaims the incomparable path to the bliss of tranquility. To those of upright intellect, your eye is surely straight, like a vessel of nectar; to those of crooked intellect, it is a vessel of nectar with its words exceedingly crooked.
He who praises you, thinking, "This is a narrative of your virtues," considers himself to be praising you.
"Surely that ocean was drunk by me through the consumption of its mouthfuls of water"—thus he understands.

Moreover, O Lord, this narrative concerning you— which describes qualities that do not even admit of being recounted by the enemies of Smara in their entirety— is a tale whose beginning is inverted and whose pride is in vain.
Thus ends the section on half-regular meters within the *Vṛttamālāvivṛti*, a commentary on the *Duṣkaraprabheda*.

O Ocean of Virtues, when the feet of the *padacaturūrdhva* consist of eight syllables that do not tolerate deep immersion due to their increasing length, and the hollows of the fingers are filled by oceans [of syllables], then compassion leads one through the unevenness of the ten stages to the state of liberation.

When the meter has been thus declared, with its arrangement of uneven feet and its adherence to the rules of light and heavy syllables, who would not feel fear— unless you are certainly free from the affliction that follows the restrictive terminology?

This bud-like row of teeth of yours, resembling the jewels in the crown of the Destroyer of Tripura, shines like a sprout from the bulbous root of wisdom long planted for the benefit of others— its formidable form fashioned for the subduing of wicked people.
Holding before you the boundless expanse of the sky as if it were a mass of fiercely terrible,
spreading fangs, even the very act of subduing is forcibly quelled by the mere play of a sidelong glance from your eyes.
Furthermore, for those of gentle nature, this very [compassion]— which has pacified the entire heap of harsh and turbid poisons—
is surely a stream of nectar that brings forth, moment by moment, a fresh and incomparable treasure of bliss.
The varieties of *padacaturūrdhva*.

O Lord, this slender body of Yours has somehow emerged victorious from somewhere, surpassing the mass of clouds that is incessantly burdened by the weight of its rising mass and made brilliant by lightning, yet possesses a terrible and deep thundering.
Therefore, as you display hundreds of such exceedingly difficult feats,
this marvelous fragrance of your potent fame gladdens the entire world.
While your body displays various distortions in its frowns, sidelong glances, and bared teeth, it subdues the worlds; yet, how strange that it is both so graceful and yet so formidable!
The non-differentiated emergences.
Even when such an extraordinary and terrifying mass of clouds, capable of destroying the world, gathers from all sides with equal intensity,
the wind, though moving with no lack of speed, playfully fails to equal your rapid pace.

O Blessed One, why should one further take refuge in you—who, having attained the incomparable state of a bull among men (*ārṣabha*), bears the burden of stability—since that very epithet of the Pure Virāj places its foot upon the head of no other rival? 150.

Having propitiated you, O Lord, through the singular excellence of my refuge, may whatever stainless merit exists and is ever-increasing cause this entire world to rise toward the vast state that is your own desire, by means of various specific modes of conduct.
Moreover, through this ever-increasing accumulation of virtue, which is exceedingly pure and stainless,
may the entire mass of darkness arising from the night of existence vanish for every embodied being.
All poisons.

Moreover, may he here experience a body that possesses unsurpassed compassion, which— like a collection of the moon’s luster— is engaged in bodiless play through the embrace of his beloved, Mature Wisdom.
Half-uneven [meter].

Through this description of various poetic meters, may the world— accumulated with the pure and auspicious light of the moonbeams— be liberated from sorrow, its lord being the companion to the cresting flame of great bliss.
// The unevenness of the feet //
The *Vṛttamālāstuti*, a classification of the difficult practices of the noble Mañjughoṣa, is completed.
This is the work of the great paṇḍita and elder Jñānaśrīmitra.
